lines.text: You're still holding that thing? Mae... it's been a month.
lines.dir: Eli leans on the counter, glances up from his phone. Not cruel, uncomfortable.

lines.text: It's her mug.
lines.dir: Maya doesn't look up at first; thumb rubs the mug. Then lifts eyes to him.

lines.text: It's a mug.
lines.dir: Eli pockets phone, small shrug, looks away.

lines.text: Crying over it won't bring her back. You need to move on.
lines.dir: He says it to the window, not to her. Avoidant.

lines.text: Inside each of us, there's a family.
lines.dir: Push through Maya's eye into the inner hearth room. Wide shot: the four emotions.

lines.text: Not the one we're born into... the one we're born with.
Hold on. "Move on"?
lines.dir: Annoyance at the round window, one brow up, pencil tapping the clipboard.

lines.text: Move on to where? On whose schedule?
Annoyance signals when small boundaries are being ignored, or minimized.
It has a laser focus for anything vague, or quietly dismissive.
Somebody should ask him. Why did you say that?
Hello? ...Anybody?
lines.dir: Nobody answers. Fear pacing, Sadness in the corner.

lines.text: HEY! She's talking! Is anybody in here even listening?!
lines.say: Hey! She's talking! Is anybody in here even listening?
lines.dir: Anger stands on his chair, head flames burst, hearth flares.

lines.text: Anger steps in when another emotion is being silenced.
It amplifies that voice, until it's heard.
lines.dir: Anger pumps the hearth bellows; fire roars.

lines.text: Name-calling. Labeling without consent. Dismissiveness. Invalidation.
lines.dir: Each word forms in the smoke above the hearth.

lines.text: Minimizing someone's lived experience, or their humanity.
Okay. Okay... I'm here. I'm listening.
lines.dir: Inner Maya (soft glow) steps in and sits at the table.

lines.text: ...Took you long enough.
lines.dir: Flames shrink; he sits, arms crossed, gruff but softened.

lines.text: What did you see?
He put a deadline on your grief.
Yeah. He did.
When the unheard voice is finally heard, Anger doesn't need to shout.
Eli... why did you say that? That I need to move on?
I don't know. Because... it's been a month.
I know you mean well.
But my grief doesn't have a deadline.
Please don't tell me how long I'm allowed to miss her.
...I can't do the sad thing, Mae.
lines.dir: Long pause; jaw works; eyes glisten.

lines.text: If I start... I don't think I'll stop.
Then we don't do it alone.
A boundary, held with care, can open a door instead of closing one.
We still have to clear out Nana's house. Saturday.
Saturday?! No. No, no, no. We can't go in that house. Not yet!
lines.say: Saturday? No. No, no, no. We can't go in that house. Not yet!

lines.text: Fear signals potential danger, or threat.
A tiger jumping out of a bush.
Or a super tall roller coaster, for the first time.
But it also watches whether our plans protect our physical and emotional safety.
Fear... who are you protecting?
Her.
lines.dir: Glances toward Sadness in the corner, then back.

lines.text: Nobody's sat with her since the funeral.
If we open that door, everything she's holding is going to pour out like water.
Fear wants our other emotions stronger and healthier, before we go.
Then before Saturday... I'll sit with her.
...That's all I wanted.
I'm sorry. I know I make everything heavy.
lines.dir: Maya sits on the floor beside her.

lines.text: You don't make it heavy. It is heavy.
You've just been the one carrying it.
I saw her hands shaking, at the end. I saw how scared she was.
Somebody has to remember that.
I remember.
Will you tell me what else you remember?
Slow down, sweet pea. Bread knows when you're rushing.
Sadness signals when part of us has been neglected. Not fully seen. Not fully heard.
It asks for deep empathy, acknowledgment, care, and comfort.
And when we give it that, it tells us we really are listening.
What does grief mean for you?
For me, my grief is my sadness,
which wants me to reflect on what those who I lost, or those who I loved... what they meant to me in my life,
because I have witnessed their suffering,
and I want to understand what their suffering meant, and means, and will mean to me in my life,
because my sadness is the emotion that helped, and helps, and will help me witness suffering in the world, and in myself,
and wants me to reflect on what the suffering means,
because if we are not there to witness it, then who bore witness to it,
to give that suffering meaning to ourselves, so that it was not meaningless?
Because my sadness does not want suffering to be meaningless,
it wants me to give that suffering meaning in my life, because those people had meaning,
and I will give them meaning by reflecting on my sadness, and what their suffering meant, and means, and will mean,
to my soul, and my life, and the world.
Mae... it's her bread recipe.
She wrote, "for my two."
Tell me what you remember.
She always said bread knows when you're rushing.
Our emotions aren't problems to fix. They're family.
And every one of them is trying to tell us what matters.
